title: Exodus Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:1, if a man steals and kills an ox, how many oxen must he restore?
options: Two oxen
Five oxen
Three oxen
Four oxen
questions.correctAnswer: Five oxen
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:1 states that if a man steals an ox and kills it, he shall restore five oxen for the ox.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 22:2, if a thief is found breaking in and is killed, the killer shall be punished.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:2 says if a thief is found breaking in and is smitten that he die, no blood shall be shed for him, so the killer is not punished.

questions.question: What happens if the sun rises on a thief who has stolen something, according to Exodus 22:3?
options: He shall be forgiven
He shall be sold for his theft
He shall be set free
He shall pay half restitution
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be sold for his theft
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:3 states that if the sun rises on a thief, there shall be blood shed for him, and if he has nothing to make restitution, he shall be sold for his theft.

questions.question: If a man is found with stolen ox, ass, or sheep alive in his hand, what must he do, according to Exodus 22:4?
options: Return it once
Restore double
Pay a fine of tenfold
Keep it without penalty
questions.correctAnswer: Restore double
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:4 commands that if the theft is found in his hand alive, he shall restore double.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 22:5 commands a man who lets his beast feed in another man's field to make restitution from the best of his own field and vineyard.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:5 instructs that if a man causes a field or vineyard to be eaten by his beast feeding there, he must make restitution from the best of his own field and vineyard.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:6, who must make restitution if fire breaks out and consumes another's crops?
options: The owner of the crops
The man who kindled the fire
The nearest neighbor
The city elders
questions.correctAnswer: The man who kindled the fire
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:6 states that if fire breaks out and consumes crops, the man who kindled the fire must make restitution.

questions.question: If money or goods are stolen from a man's house while he is keeping them for his neighbor, what must happen if the thief is found, according to Exodus 22:7?
options: The thief pays back the original amount
The thief pays double
The owner loses the goods
The neighbor must forgive the loss
questions.correctAnswer: The thief pays double
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:7 commands that if money or goods are stolen and the thief is found, he must pay double.

questions.question: True or False: If the thief is not found, the master of the house shall be taken to the judges to determine if he stole, as per Exodus 22:8.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:8 says if the thief is not found, the master of the house shall be brought before judges to see if he has taken his neighbor's goods.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:9, what must be done if a judge condemns someone for a trespass regarding lost or stolen goods?
options: They pay half the value
They pay double to their neighbor
They are imprisoned
They are fined without restitution
questions.correctAnswer: They pay double to their neighbor
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:9 states that the person condemned by judges shall pay double to their neighbor.

questions.question: If a man delivers an animal to his neighbor to keep and it dies or is hurt without witnesses, what shall happen according to Exodus 22:10?
options: The keeper must pay damages
An oath of the LORD shall be between them
The owner must accept loss
The animal must be replaced
questions.correctAnswer: An oath of the LORD shall be between them
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:10 states that if an animal dies or is hurt with no witness, an oath of the LORD shall be between the parties.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:11, if the keeper swears he did not touch the neighbor's goods, what must the owner do?
options: He shall demand full payment
He shall accept the oath and not require repayment
He shall seek further judgment
He shall sell the goods
questions.correctAnswer: He shall accept the oath and not require repayment
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:11 commands that the owner shall accept the oath and not require the keeper to make good the loss.

questions.question: Which of the following comes first according to the order of instructions in Exodus 22?
options: Restitution for stolen oxen
Rules about fire damage
Consequences for a thief caught breaking in
Instructions about lending money without interest
questions.correctAnswer: Restitution for stolen oxen
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:1 begins with restitution for stolen oxen and sheep, which comes before rules about fire damage (v6), thief consequences (v2-3), and lending rules (v25).

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 22:3, if a thief cannot make restitution, he shall be sold for his theft.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:3 states that if the thief has nothing to make restitution, he shall be sold for his theft.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:4, what animals are mentioned as examples that if found stolen alive in a thief's hand require double restitution?
options: Ox, ass, sheep
Horse, goat, ox
Sheep, goat, camel
Ox, camel, donkey
questions.correctAnswer: Ox, ass, sheep
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:4 mentions ox, ass, and sheep as animals which if found alive in a thief's hand require double restitution.

questions.question: If a man causes fire to consume another's field or stacks of corn, what must he do according to Exodus 22:6?
options: He must pay half damages
He must make full restitution
He must be put to death
He must be fined by the elders
questions.correctAnswer: He must make full restitution
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:6 states that the man who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution for the damage caused.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:12, what must a man do if an animal he was keeping for a neighbor is stolen from him?
options: He shall make restitution unto the owner thereof
He shall swear an oath before the LORD
He shall not make it good
He shall pay double to the owner
questions.correctAnswer: He shall make restitution unto the owner thereof
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:12 clearly states that if the animal is stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the owner. This complements Exodus 22:10–11 which deal with the responsibility when the animal dies or is hurt, indicating the importance of making things right.

questions.question: What is the requirement if an animal lent to a neighbor is torn in pieces, according to Exodus 22?
options: The lender must bring the torn pieces as a witness and the borrower does not have to make good that which was torn
The borrower must pay double the value of the animal
The lender must accept the loss without compensation
The borrower must replace the animal
questions.correctAnswer: The lender must bring the torn pieces as a witness and the borrower does not have to make good that which was torn
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:13 teaches that if the animal is torn, the owner must bring it as evidence, and the borrower is not required to compensate for what was torn. This ties to the principle in Exodus 22:10–11 about responsibility when no one sees the harm.

questions.question: If a man borrows something from his neighbor, and it is hurt or dies while the owner is not present, what does Exodus 22:14 command?
options: He shall surely make it good
He shall not be responsible
He shall swear an oath of innocence
He shall give a replacement item
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely make it good
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:14 commands the borrower to make good for the loss if the owner is not with the borrowed item, emphasizing accountability in stewardship. This complements Exodus 22:15 where the responsibility changes if the owner is present.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:15, what happens if the owner is with the borrowed item and it is hurt or dies?
options: The borrower shall not make it good
The borrower must pay double
The borrower must replace the item
The owner is responsible for the loss
questions.correctAnswer: The borrower shall not make it good
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:15 states that if the owner is with the item, the borrower is not liable because the item was under the owner's watch, teaching fairness in responsibility. This contrasts with verse 14 where the owner is absent.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:16 say a man must do if he entices a maid who is not betrothed and lies with her?
options: He shall surely endow her to be his wife
He shall pay a fine to her father
He shall leave her without marriage
He shall offer a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: He shall surely endow her to be his wife
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:16 prescribes that the man must endow the maid to be his wife, demonstrating the value of commitment and responsibility in relationships. Verse 17 further explains the procedure if her father refuses.

questions.question: If the father refuses to give his daughter to the man who enticed her, what is he required to do according to Exodus 22:17?
options: He shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins
He shall marry her anyway
He shall pay double restitution
He shall be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: He shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:17 states that if the father refuses, the man must pay money equivalent to a virgin's dowry, showing the law's concern for fairness and provision. This follows the instruction in verse 16 about marriage.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:18 command about witches?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:18 explicitly commands that a witch shall not be suffered to live. This reflects the seriousness with which such practices were regarded in this law code.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:19, what is the penalty for lying with a beast?
options: Death
A fine
Exile
Restitution twice over
questions.correctAnswer: Death
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:19 clearly states that anyone who lies with a beast shall surely be put to death, emphasizing the severity of this offense in the law.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:20 declare about sacrifices to any god except the LORD?
options: He shall be utterly destroyed
He shall be forgiven if he repents
He shall pay a fine
He shall offer a substitute sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: He shall be utterly destroyed
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:20 pronounces that anyone sacrificing to gods other than the LORD shall be utterly destroyed, underscoring exclusive worship of the LORD in Israel.

questions.question: How does Exodus 22:21 teach about treatment of strangers?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:21 commands not to vex or oppress a stranger, reminding the Israelites they were once strangers in Egypt, teaching empathy and kindness.

questions.question: What warning does Exodus 22:23 give if widows or fatherless children are afflicted and cry out to God?
options: God will surely hear their cry
Their cry will go unanswered
They must bring their complaint before judges only
They must seek revenge themselves
questions.correctAnswer: God will surely hear their cry
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:23 promises that if widows or orphans are afflicted and cry to God, He will surely hear their cry, emphasizing God's care for the vulnerable.

questions.question: What consequence does Exodus 22:24 say will come upon those who afflict widows or fatherless children?
options: God's wrath will burn hot and they will be killed with the sword
They will be fined by the judges
They will be cast out of the community
They will be forgiven if they repent
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath will burn hot and they will be killed with the sword
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:24 warns that God's wrath will ignite and He will kill those who afflict widows or fatherless children, showing the seriousness of such injustice.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:25, how should one lend money to the poor among God's people?
options: Without charging interest or usury
With a standard interest rate
Only with collateral
With double repayment
questions.correctAnswer: Without charging interest or usury
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:25 instructs lenders not to act as usurers or charge interest to the poor among God's people, highlighting generosity and compassion in lending.

questions.question: What must be done if a neighbor’s garment is taken as a pledge, according to Exodus 22:26–27?
options: It must be returned to him by sunset because it is his only covering
It can be kept until the debt is repaid
It must be sold to pay the debt
It must be burned if the debt is not paid
questions.correctAnswer: It must be returned to him by sunset because it is his only covering
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:26–27 commands that a neighbor's garment taken as a pledge must be returned by sunset since it is his only covering, demonstrating concern for human dignity and basic needs.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:28 forbid regarding gods and rulers?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:28 forbids reviling the gods or cursing the ruler of the people, so the statement that it permits cursing is false.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:23-24, what consequence does God promise if widows and fatherless children are afflicted and cry out to Him?
options: God will ignore their cry
God will hear their cry and bring wrath upon the oppressors
God will forgive the oppressors
God will send prophets to warn the oppressors
questions.correctAnswer: God will hear their cry and bring wrath upon the oppressors
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:23-24 states that if widows and fatherless children are afflicted and cry to God, He will surely hear their cry and His wrath will be kindled against the oppressors, leading to their destruction.

questions.question: What instruction does Exodus 22:25 give regarding lending money to the poor among God's people?
options: Lend with interest to ensure repayment
Lend without charging usury or interest
Do not lend money at all
Only lend money to strangers
questions.correctAnswer: Lend without charging usury or interest
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:25 commands that when lending money to the poor among God's people, one must not act as an usurer or charge interest, showing compassion and fairness.

questions.question: In Exodus 22:26-27, what is the reason given for returning a neighbor’s raiment by sunset if taken as a pledge?
options: Because it is valuable property
Because it is his covering and he needs it to sleep
Because it is a symbol of friendship
Because it is required by the judges
questions.correctAnswer: Because it is his covering and he needs it to sleep
questions.explanation: Verse 27 explains that the raiment is the only covering for the neighbor’s skin, necessary for sleeping, so it must be returned by sunset to show mercy and compassion.

questions.question: Which of the following is prohibited according to Exodus 22:28?
options: Reviling the gods and cursing the ruler of the people
Eating meat torn by beasts
Charging interest on loans to the poor
Stealing oxen or sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Reviling the gods and cursing the ruler of the people
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:28 explicitly forbids reviling gods and cursing the ruler of the people, emphasizing respect for divine and human authorities.

questions.question: What is commanded in Exodus 22:29 regarding offerings to the LORD?
options: Delay offerings until harvest is complete
Offer the first of ripe fruits and liquors, and give the firstborn sons to God
Offer only animals, not fruits
Give offerings only during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Offer the first of ripe fruits and liquors, and give the firstborn sons to God
questions.explanation: Verse 29 instructs the Israelites not to delay offerings but to give the first ripe fruits, liquors, and the firstborn sons to God, symbolizing dedication and gratitude.

questions.question: Exodus 22:30 instructs the people to give oxen and sheep to God after how many days?
options: Seven days with the dam, eighth day to God
Immediately after birth
After one month
After the first year
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days with the dam, eighth day to God
questions.explanation: The verse commands that oxen and sheep remain with their mother for seven days, and on the eighth day they are to be given to God, reflecting ritual purity and dedication.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:31 command regarding eating meat torn by beasts, and what should be done with such flesh?
options: It is lawful to eat it if cooked properly
It is forbidden to eat it and it must be given to dogs
It should be burnt immediately
It should be buried in the field
questions.correctAnswer: It is forbidden to eat it and it must be given to dogs
questions.explanation: Verse 31 commands holiness by prohibiting eating flesh torn by beasts and instructs that such meat should be cast to the dogs, symbolizing impurity.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the concern for protecting widows and orphans as seen in Exodus 22:22-23?
options: Deuteronomy 10:18
Genesis 12:1
Leviticus 19:18
Numbers 6:24-26
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 10:18
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 10:18 echoes the theme by stating that God defends the cause of the fatherless and widow, reinforcing the protective command found in Exodus 22:22-23.

questions.question: How does the prohibition against charging usury in Exodus 22:25 relate to teachings in the New Testament?
options: It is contradicted by Jesus’ parables
It is affirmed by teachings on generosity and love for neighbors
It is not mentioned in the New Testament
It is replaced by new economic laws
questions.correctAnswer: It is affirmed by teachings on generosity and love for neighbors
questions.explanation: The New Testament (e.g., Luke 6:34-35) affirms generosity and forbids exploitation, aligning with Exodus 22:25's prohibition against usury toward the poor.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning is important for understanding 'usury' in Exodus 22:25, and what does it imply?
options: Ribbit, meaning interest or excess charge
Kedesh, meaning holiness
Shalom, meaning peace
Chesed, meaning lovingkindness
questions.correctAnswer: Ribbit, meaning interest or excess charge
questions.explanation: 'Ribbit' is the Hebrew term for interest or usury, implying an unfair financial burden on the poor, which Exodus 22:25 forbids.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Exodus 22:23-24 to emphasize God's wrath against oppressors?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Alliteration
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:23-24 uses parallelism by juxtaposing the cry of the afflicted with God’s wrath and judgment, highlighting the cause and effect relationship.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 22:18 commands that a witch should be allowed to live if she repents.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:18 clearly states that a witch shall not be allowed to live, with no provision for repentance mentioned in this verse.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 22:20 forbids sacrificing to any god except the LORD, with the consequence of utter destruction for disobedience.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 commands exclusive sacrifice to the LORD alone and states that anyone sacrificing to other gods shall be utterly destroyed, emphasizing monotheistic worship.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the principle of caring for the stranger expressed in Exodus 22:21?
options: Matthew 25:35
John 3:16
Acts 2:38
Romans 8:28
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 25:35
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:35 highlights welcoming strangers as serving Christ Himself, echoing the command in Exodus 22:21 not to vex or oppress strangers.

questions.question: In Exodus 22:16-17, what is the prescribed action if a man entices a virgin who is not betrothed and lies with her, and her father refuses to give her to him?
options: The man must pay money according to the dowry of virgins
The man must marry another woman
The man must leave the city
The man is to be put to death
questions.correctAnswer: The man must pay money according to the dowry of virgins
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 instruct that if the father refuses to give his daughter, the man must pay a dowry to compensate, showing the value placed on marriage agreements.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:1 teach about restitution for theft of livestock?
options: The thief must restore double the value
The thief must restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep
The thief is forgiven after confession
The thief must pay a fine to the priest
questions.correctAnswer: The thief must restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:1 states that if a man steals and kills or sells an ox or sheep, he must restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep, teaching a principle of disproportionate restitution to compensate loss.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the law in Exodus 22:2 regarding the defense against a breaking thief?
options: God's mercy
God's justice
God's omniscience
God's patience
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:2 shows God's justice by permitting the defender to kill a thief caught breaking in at night without bloodguilt, reflecting God's righteous judgment on crime and protection of life.

questions.question: According to Exodus 22:5, what principle about responsibility and restitution is taught when one's animals damage another's field or vineyard?
options: The offender must offer a sacrifice
Restitution must be made from the best of his own field and vineyard
The owner of the field bears the loss
The case must be taken to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: Restitution must be made from the best of his own field and vineyard
questions.explanation: Verse 5 commands that if a man's animals feed in another's field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field and vineyard, indicating personal responsibility and justice in restitution.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is highlighted by Exodus 22:21-24 concerning treatment of strangers, widows, and orphans?
options: Sanctification of the believer
God's covenantal justice and care for the vulnerable
Predestination of the elect
The doctrine of atonement
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenantal justice and care for the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:21-24 reveals God's justice and covenantal concern by commanding kindness and protection for strangers, widows, and orphans, promising that He hears their cries and will punish oppressors.

questions.question: How does Exodus 22:16-17 contribute to the biblical understanding of marriage and social responsibility?
options: By requiring a public ceremony for marriage
By mandating endowment or dowry payment for a virgin enticed
By prohibiting marriage outside the tribe
By allowing polygamy for wealthy men
questions.correctAnswer: By mandating endowment or dowry payment for a virgin enticed
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 teach that a man who entices an unbetrothed maid must endow her as his wife or pay a dowry if the father refuses, emphasizing social responsibility and protection in marriage arrangements.

questions.question: What does Exodus 22:18 reveal about the holiness and purity demanded by God in Israelite society?
options: Witches are to be integrated into the community
Witches are to be tolerated
Witches are not to be suffered to live
Witches are to be exiled
questions.correctAnswer: Witches are not to be suffered to live
questions.explanation: Verse 18 commands that a witch shall not be suffered to live, reflecting God's demand for holiness and rejection of occult practices that defile His covenant people.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about restitution and justice can be drawn from Exodus 22:4 and Exodus 22:7?
options: Restitution must always be triple the loss
The thief must be forgiven upon repentance
Restitution includes paying double for theft or loss when found
Restitution is optional based on the victim's mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Restitution includes paying double for theft or loss when found
questions.explanation: Both verses 4 and 7 require the thief or the one who caused loss to pay double restitution when the stolen property or thief is found, emphasizing God's demand for justice and full compensation.

questions.question: What is the significance of the oath described in Exodus 22:11 in the context of property disputes?
options: It removes the need for restitution
It establishes a divine guarantee of innocence
It allows the owner to seize the property
It requires the judge to decide without evidence
questions.correctAnswer: It establishes a divine guarantee of innocence
questions.explanation: Verse 11 explains that an oath of the LORD between parties establishes innocence regarding property damage when no witness is present, showing reliance on divine truth in justice.

questions.question: How does Exodus 22:25-27 demonstrate God's attribute of grace toward the poor?
options: By forbidding lending money to the poor
By commanding interest on loans to the poor
By prohibiting usury and requiring prompt return of pledged garments
By allowing seizure of all collateral
questions.correctAnswer: By prohibiting usury and requiring prompt return of pledged garments
questions.explanation: Verses 25-27 forbid charging interest to the poor and require returning pledged garments by sunset, illustrating God's gracious care and compassion for vulnerable neighbors.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Exodus 22:29-30 have with the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It introduces the idea of animal sacrifices as a means of atonement
It prescribes dietary laws unrelated to redemption
It emphasizes firstfruits and firstborn dedicated to God, foreshadowing Christ as the firstborn
It forbids eating meat altogether
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes firstfruits and firstborn dedicated to God, foreshadowing Christ as the firstborn
questions.explanation: Verses 29-30 command offering first fruits and firstborn to God, connecting to the redemptive theme where Christ is the firstborn and firstfruits of resurrection (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:20).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about sanctification is taught by Exodus 22:31 concerning eating meat torn by beasts?
options: Believers may eat any meat without restriction
Believers must be holy and avoid eating meat torn by beasts
Meat torn by beasts is considered a delicacy
The law permits eating of all animals
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must be holy and avoid eating meat torn by beasts
questions.explanation: Verse 31 commands Israel to be holy and not eat meat torn by beasts, teaching separation from defilement and the call to holiness in daily life.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Exodus 22:10 and Exodus 22:14 provide about responsibility for borrowed property?
options: Borrowed property is considered lost if damaged
Borrower must make restitution if property is hurt or dies when owner is not present
Owner is always responsible for loss
Borrower is exempt from all liability
questions.correctAnswer: Borrower must make restitution if property is hurt or dies when owner is not present
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 14 teach that if borrowed property is hurt or dies while the owner is absent, the borrower must make it good, showing personal accountability in stewardship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Old Testament laws promote harsh retribution and lack divine mercy. What does Exodus 22:23-24 actually teach about God's response to oppression?
options: God ignores the cries of the oppressed
God is indifferent to human suffering
God hears the cries of the oppressed and will bring just wrath on oppressors
God always forgives oppressors without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God hears the cries of the oppressed and will bring just wrath on oppressors
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 affirm that when widows or fatherless children cry out due to affliction, God hears and responds with righteous judgment, highlighting His justice and mercy.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by combining Exodus 22:21 and Exodus 22:25 about God's covenantal expectations?
options: God expects His people to oppress strangers and charge interest
God commands kindness to strangers and forbids usury among His people
God allows exploitation of the poor and strangers
God's covenant is only about worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: God commands kindness to strangers and forbids usury among His people
questions.explanation: Verses 21 and 25 together teach that God's covenant demands kindness to strangers and prohibits charging interest to the poor, reflecting God's justice and compassion.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in Exodus 22:27 through His promise to hear the cry of one who has lost his covering?
options: Omnipotence
Holiness
Graciousness
Wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Graciousness
questions.explanation: Verse 27 highlights God's graciousness as He promises to hear the cry of one who has lost his raiment, showing His tender care for the needy.
